reading.rtitle: Brightwave Retail · Account Plan · Next Fiscal Year · Prepared by Patrícia
paras: Brightwave renewed in October, and this plan describes what we want to achieve together in the next fiscal year. The main goal is expansion. Today the platform is used in forty stores, and the forecast is that Brightwave will open twenty more by the end of the year. The plan has three phases, and each phase ends with a checkpoint call with Daniel and his finance team.

Phase one starts with a kickoff in January. By the end of February, we will have moved the twelve stores in the new region to the platform. In March, our team will be training the store managers in small groups, so the support line will be busier than usual. Phase two is the go-live of the mobile app in May. By then, every store manager will have received a login, and from June we will be sending Daniel a weekly usage report.

Phase three is our stretch goal: the twenty new stores. If the openings are on time, sixty stores will have joined the platform by December, and if they are ahead of schedule, we will add an extra checkpoint in September. The only real risk is the budget: finance will be reviewing all software costs in June, so the checkpoint before that date is the most important one of the year. This time next year, we will be preparing the next renewal with numbers, not promises.
reading.source: Adapted for class use from a customer success account plan

gist.prompt: What is the best one-line summary of this document?
choices: A report about what went wrong with Brightwave last year.
A plan for next year: three phases of expansion, with dates, checkpoints and one risk.
A proposal to give Brightwave a discount for the new stores.

The plan ends with numbers, not promises. Which number would you like to show your customer this time next year?

listenings.text: Hi Patrícia, it is Karen. I read the Brightwave account plan. It is the best one in the team, and I want to use it as an example. One small suggestion before you send it. In each phase, write one sentence with a date and a result, like: by the end of February, we will have moved twelve stores. Customers remember dates, not activities. Then, for the busy months, say what your team will be doing, so that the customer knows what to expect. And please add the forecast for the twenty new stores, even if it is not certain. A number with a risk is better than no number. Send it to Daniel before the checkpoint on Friday, and copy me.

Hi Patrícia, it is Arjun, about the Brightwave plan. I checked the technical side, and most of it is realistic. By the end of January, we will have finished the tests for the new region, so February is fine for the move. The mobile app is the tight part. In April, my team will be fixing the last bugs, so the go-live in May is possible, but not early. Please do not promise that we will be ahead of schedule there. One more thing: by the time the twenty new stores open, the nightly file will have doubled again. I will be watching the sync closely, and the alert will tell you if anything is slow.
